items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the insurance law, in relation to discounting uninsured dental services
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S6496

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the insurance law, in relation to
discounting uninsured dental services

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

To prevent insurance companies from including in their contracts any
provisions that relate to or affect dental services that they do not
insure.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Section 1 prevents an insurance or managed care company from including
in any insurance or managed care contract any provisions that relate
to or affect dental services that are not covered by the contract.

Section 2 makes the bill effective January 1, 2018, and applicable to
any insurance or managed care contracts issued or entered into on or
after that date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Existing New York State Insurance Law - Section 4224(d)(1) of the
Insurance Law - prohibits interdependent sales whereby an insurer puts
into its insurance policies products or services that are not insured
as a means of interdependently selling that policy and the uninsured
items to its insureds. Some insurers are routinely flouting that law
by including in their dental plans discounts on dental services they
do not insure and then requiring dentists to provide such discounts in
order to be a participating provider in the dental insurance plan. In
effect, the insurer subsidizes the sale of its insurance plan to
patients by using money from dentists offered in the form of discounts
on uninsured dental services. Simultaneously, the insurer is selling
that discount product to patients as part of the insurance policy as
an inducement to buy the insurance policy.  This pernicious marketing
practice to sell dental insurance plans by coupling them to discounts
on uninsured dental services has been allowed to continue because
regulators have had difficulty distinguishing between insured and
uninsured dental services. The bill makes it clear that no insurer can
place into their contracts any provisions relating to dental services
that they do not insure.

This bill is necessary to restore sensible enforcement of the law
against interdependent sales with respect to dental insurance plans.
Many other states have outlawed this practice directly in a similar
way, using the logic that dental insurers should not be influencing
the prices or other aspects of dental services that they do not insure
at all and never pay for. However, New York does not need this logic,
compelling though it is, because New York long ago prevented
interdependent sales schemes in insurance plans and this law merely
clarifies that it applies to uninsured dental services as it would to
any other improper interdependent sales scheme. Several dental
insurers, including Cigna and Delta Dental, do not engage in this
practice in New York in recognition of the pernicious aspects of doing
so. The law is timed to take effect on January 1, 2018, and only to
apply to insurance or managed care contracts issued or entered into on
or after that date.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

None.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None to the state.
 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on January 1, 2018, and apply to insurance
and managed care contracts issued or entered into on or after that
date.

summary: Prevents an insurance or managed care company from including in any insurance or managed care contract any provisions that require a dentist to provide services to a covered person at a fee set by or at a fee subject to the approval of the insurer or managed care entity unless such services are covered under the person's dental plan.
title: Relates to discounting uninsured dental services

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 237
 
TO THE SENATE:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:
 
Senate Bill Number 6496-A, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to amend the insurance law, in relation to discounting unin-
      sured dental services"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  With certain exceptions, insurance companies are not required to offer
dental benefits in any health insurance policies and contracts issued in
the  State.  As  a  result,  individuals often purchase their own dental
plans to cover these services. To manage costs for their  covered  indi-
viduals,  insurers  often  include  provisions  in  their  policies with
dentists to require them to provide certain services at discounted pric-
es, even if the services are not  covered  by  the  individual's  dental
plan.

  This bill would end this practice and prohibit insurers from mandating
prices  to  dentists for services that are not covered under an individ-
ual's plan. However, providing dental discounts for non-covered services
allows an individual to have access  to  necessary  dental  care  at  an
affordable  rate.  As  this  bill  would  limit  cost-saving benefits to
consumers, and thereby potentially eliminate access to dental  services,
I am constrained to veto this bill.
 
  The bill is disapproved.                    (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
 
                               __________
